question: Vectors whose lines of action meet at one point are called:
explanation: Concurrent vectors are those whose lines of action all intersect at a single common point [Vectors and Scalars].

question: Concurrent vectors all meet at the same:
explanation: By definition, concurrent vectors intersect or meet at the same place or point [Vectors and Scalars].

question: A scalar quantity has:

options.A: Numerical size of the quantity only
options.C: Both direction and numerical size of the quantity

explanation: Scalar quantities are fully described by magnitude (size) alone without any directional component [Vectors and Scalars].

question:
Find the magnitude and direction of 3 coplanar forces of:
1. 40 N 45° east of south
2. 10 N west
3. 70 N 35° east of north
explanation: Summing horizontal (X) and vertical (Y) components yields $\Sigma X = 58.43$ N and $\Sigma Y = 29.06$ N. The resultant magnitude is $\sqrt{58.43^2 + 29.06^2} \approx 65$ N directed approximately 60° east of north [Vectors and Scalars].

question: A vector quantity has:

options.A: Both direction and necessary units of the quantity
options.B: Magnitude and necessary units of the quantity
options.C: Both numerical size and the necessary units of the quantity
options.E: Direction, magnitude, and necessary units of the quantity

explanation: A vector quantity is completely specified by its magnitude, direction, and appropriate units [Vectors and Scalars].

question: Coplanar vectors all occur in the same:
explanation: Coplanar vectors lie within the exact same two-dimensional plane [Vectors and Scalars].

question:
Find the magnitude and direction of 4 concurrent coplanar forces:

1. 10 N 32° east of north
2. 35 N 50° east of north
3. 25 N 72° east of north
4. 85 N 40° east of south
explanation: Resolving all forces into X and Y axes gives $\Sigma X = 110.53$ N and $\Sigma Y = -26.42$ N. The resultant magnitude is $\sqrt{110.53^2 + (-26.42)^2} \approx 114$ N at an angle of 77° east of south [Vectors and Scalars].

question: With reference to scalars and vectors, a space diagram:

options.B: Illustrates the position of the planets and stars
options.C: Shows the relationship of the scalar to the vector
options.E: Shows the relationship of time to the vector

explanation: A space diagram visually represents physical bodies and the system of vectors acting upon them in space [Vectors and Scalars].

question: The resultant of a system of vectors is:

options.A: Equal to the smallest vector in the system
options.B: The single vector that can replace the system of vectors
options.C: The sum of the magnitudes of the system vectors
options.D: Equal to the largest vector in the system
options.E: The single vector that can replace the system of vectors and have the same effect

explanation: The resultant vector is a single vector that produces exactly the same overall effect on a body as the original system of vectors combined [Vectors and Scalars].

question: Displacement is:

options.D: Measured by the actual path the object travels
options.E: How far an object has moved

explanation: Displacement has both magnitude (straight-line distance) and a specific direction from start to finish, making it a vector quantity [Vectors and Scalars].
